answer: Randomness-gated admission kernel. Each epoch, a public verifiable random beacon seeds a permutation; only agents whose identity hash falls in a fresh threshold window gain admission, and the seed is revealed post-commitment so attackers cannot precompute positions. The kernel rotates admissions unpredictably, forcing a sybil to create and maintain many dormant identities that may never activate. Timber for signatures and a prism-based commitment log let anyone verify the permutation was unbiased, so forged identities cost real compute and storage per slot with no guarantee of use,
